subject: Critical Thinking
title: Black Swans: The Impacts We Can't Predict
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Black Swans: The Impacts We Can't Predict.

hook.text: Before 1697, Europeans were certain all swans were white. Then they reached Australia.

buildup.text: Nassim Taleb's Black Swans: rare, unpredictable events with massive consequences that we rationalize after the fact.

discovery.text: 9/11, the internet, COVID-19, the iPhone — all Black Swans. None were predicted. All changed the world.

punchline.text: The thing that changes everything is the thing you didn't see coming.

quiz.question: What characterizes a Black Swan event?
options: It's rare, unpredictable, and has massive consequences

details.summary: Nassim Taleb's Black Swans are events that are rare, have extreme impact, and are retrospectively predictable but not prospectively. The 2008 financial crisis and the internet's rise are examples of events that reshape the world.
details.whyItMatters: Black Swans show that the most important events in history are precisely the ones nobody predicted, undermining confidence in forecasting and risk models.
takeaways: Black Swans are rare, impactful, and rationalized only in hindsight
Standard risk models underestimate extreme events catastrophically
Positioning for Black Swans is more useful than predicting them

faq.question: What are the three characteristics of a Black Swan event?
faq.answer: It is an outlier beyond normal expectations, it has an extreme impact, and after it occurs, people construct explanations that make it seem predictable in hindsight. All three features must be present.

faq.question: How can you position yourself to benefit from positive Black Swans?
faq.answer: Taleb recommends a barbell strategy: keep most resources safe from negative Black Swans while making small, diverse bets that could benefit enormously from positive ones. Limit downside while keeping upside open.
